newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz sees clear rise in 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Allianz sees clear rise in 1996 profit.

text.p: German insurance giant Allianz AG Holding on Thursday predicted its 1996 group pre-tax earnings would rise significantly after premium income rose 7.6 percent to 56.2 billion marks in the first nine months.

However, Allianz said in a statement that the profit rise would not match that achieved last year since it would not have the tax benefits connected to its takeover of East German insurer Deutsche Versicherungs AG which boosted 1995 earnings.
The group said its improved earnings were due to a systematic risk selection and favourable claims experience in many markets, together with the absence of major natural catastrophes.
Personnel and administrative expenses had also been curbed by improved working procedures and cost control measures.

"All things considered, the underwriting result will be higher than last year's figure. Non-underwriting business has benefited from the benign climate on capital markets, making it possible to realise increased gains and investment income has risen," Allianz said.
However lower interest rates have lowered the returns on new investments, the statement added.

On premium income developments, Allianz said the strengthening of major foreign currencies this year had added 1.4 billion marks to its earnings in the first nine months while changes in its group structure had cut earnings by 200 million marks.

Allianz this year consolidated its Swiss Berner insurance group and credit insurer Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG while its health insurance unit Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG left the group on July 31, 1996.
Without the changes in currencies and structure, group premium income would have risen 5.3 percent, Allianz said.
Life and health insurance business rose 9.2 percent in the nine-month period, with German life business showing particular improvement.
In addition, single premium variable annuity insurance business resumed its advance in the U.S. and Italian business also improved. Non-life business, however, rose just 2.7 percent.
Staff levels dropped by 5.1 percent to 65,500 as at September 30.
